sample_unit: observations (model responses to 200 items across 4 trials x 3 models)

links.outcome: Output consistency of LLM answers across four repeated trials on orthodontic diagnostic items
links.effect: Consistency differed by model: most accurate model (Claude, 99.0% accuracy) was least consistent (93.0%); least accurate (ChatGPT, 94.0%) was second-most consistent (98.0%).
links.quote: An accuracy–consistency paradox emerged: the most accurate model was the least consistent (93.0%), while the least accurate was the second-most consistent (98.0%).

unlisted_practices: Context-rich prompting versus standard prompting to eliminate errors on synthetic data (40 items, 480 observations)
Repeated-trial evaluation to expose stochasticity concealed by single-trial testing

screen.practice: context-rich prompting and repeated-trial consistency evaluation
screen.reason: The study empirically tests frontier LLMs on orthodontic diagnostic tasks across repeated trials and evaluates the effect of a prompt engineering safeguard (context-rich prompting) on accuracy and consistency.
